unavailableMetrics: Non-follower reach not exposed by connected Buffer metrics.
Facebook post-attributed follows, saves, views and watch time not exposed. Null means unavailable, not zero.
performance.interpretation: Reels provide far more observed reach than carousels or stills but the mature seven-day cohort generated zero Instagram follows. This is not evidence of improved audience growth. Format groups are small and observational, not randomized. Historical change/conflict/mystery/stakes caption generated 12 follows; repeat its reader need, not its media or wording.
performance.decision: Stop repeating generic binary resource-crisis carousels and static ominous-door hooks after multiple comparable low-reach, zero-follow posts. Retain 11/17/20 format mix while changing creative hypothesis: progressive architectural scale reveal, warm visual-search family reveal, and serial character agency with a concrete payoff. Do not extend the same low-performing pattern blindly.
performance.nextEvaluation: Evaluate these posts only once 24 hours old. Prioritize follows and non-follower reach if available, then shares/saves/comments; compare against mature baseline. Do not interpret scheduled status as publication or growth.

pieces.subject: Highward's Hidden Foundation
alt: Highward, capital of Varren, revealed in three views from human-scale houses to the colossal Vanir ruin beneath the city.
pieces.ig:
A home to you. A ruin to history.

At street level, Highward looks like a city built by people. Follow the stone past the houses and the scale stops making sense.

Varren's capital stands on an enormous Vanir ruin. Watch the final view: would you want to know what your home was built on?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt
pieces.fb:
What if your whole city was someone else's ruin?

Highward is the capital of Varren, far south of Roo. From its streets, the houses can hide the truth. From a distance, the enormous Vanir structure beneath the city becomes unmistakable.

A familiar home, built into a past its inhabitants cannot fully explain. Watch the last view—would knowing what lies beneath make you feel safer, or less safe?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt

pieces.subject: That Is Moss, Not a Tree
alt: A smiling blond child in a wool coat and red mitten peeks through unusually large feather moss in a lush Roo forest.
The wider view reveals the same child laughing beside her mother, who holds her hand on a fallen birch beside the enormous moss.
pieces.ig:
That is moss. Not a tree.

In Roo, even the smallest things grow on a different scale. For a child, a patch of moss can become a whole hiding place.

Swipe for the wider view. She was right beside her mother all along.

What did you spot first: mitten or face?

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt
pieces.fb:
A whole hiding place in a patch of moss.

Roo's forests are unusually fertile: even their moss and mushrooms grow larger. This little scene imagines what that means on an ordinary walk with a child.

A red mitten appears above the green. The next image reveals her mother was right there, ready to take her hand.

Look at both images—what caught your eye first, the mitten or her face?

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt

pieces.subject: Fireside Tales of Roo — She Burned the Drawing
alt: A resolute blond woman in a blue embroidered dress and fur mantle uses iron tongs to burn a stranger's drawing of a dark doorway in a snowbound inn's fireplace.
pieces.ig:
She refused to follow the stranger's drawing.

At a snowbound inn, a stranger drew the door she kept seeing in her dreams. Tonight she fed his drawing to the fire.

For the first time, the choice felt like hers.

Fireside Tales of Roo: the paper is gone. Will the door still be there when she sleeps?

Follow for the next part.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #FantasyBooks #FantasyArt
pieces.fb:
Burning the drawing was the easy part.

In the previous Fireside Tales of Roo scene, a stranger at a snowbound inn drew a door the woman recognized from her dreams.

Tonight, she chooses not to follow his lead. She lowers the drawing into the fire and watches the doorway blacken. Whatever the stranger wanted, she has made one decision for herself.

But paper burns more easily than a dream. Will the door still be there when she falls asleep?

Follow the continuing Fireside Tales of Roo.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.
#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #FantasyBooks #FantasyArt

generationPrompts: Use case: illustration-story. Original cinematic Nordic fantasy concept art for The Land of Roo. Vertical 9:16, 1080x1920 composition. First scene of a visual journey in Highward, capital of Varren, a medieval city built atop enormous ancient Vanir ruins. At street level: narrow human-scale medieval limestone and half-timbered houses, slate roofs, an empty wooden handcart with a small broken wheel, rain-wet cobbles, warm early dawn light. Beneath the ordinary houses, ONE strange immense smooth pale stone rib emerges from the cobbled ground and curves upward, mostly hidden by human construction. Intriguing close eye-level composition with the huge rib as focal point, inviting the viewer to follow it. Refined realistic painterly illustration, tactile material detail, luminous cream limestone, slate blue shadows, rust-red awnings. No people, no creatures, no skulls, no runic writing, no logos or text. Not generic castle scenery, no magical glow. Keep top 15% comparatively quiet for added editorial title. This is new artwork, not a reuse of any reference.

Use case: illustration-story. Original cinematic Nordic fantasy concept art for The Land of Roo. Vertical 9:16. Second view of Highward, Varren: camera has followed an enormous smooth pale stone architectural rib out through a gap in ordinary medieval limestone and half-timbered houses with slate roofs and rust-red awnings. The foreground has a small wooden handcart and ordinary human-sized doorway for scale; behind it the pale stone rib joins a colossal ancient arch, dozens of meters high, whose upper section disappears UNDER and BEHIND the human city buildings. Reveal the discrepancy of scale without magical glow. Early dawn golden cream highlights, slate blue shadows, rain-wet stone. Photorealistic painterly, monumental precise coherent load-bearing architecture, phone-legible. No people or creatures, no inscriptions/text/logos. Top 15% quiet.

Its pale smooth stone base forms an unmistakable coherent immense circular ring and repeated gigantic arch supports, partly buried into a hillside. Human city is small and irregular, ancient foundation huge and precise. Show the whole base plainly at phone size, not a modern spaceship, not glowing, no futuristic metal. This is ancient stone architecture reused by human builders. Early dawn gold on cream stone and blue shadows, a small empty abandoned cart in foreground gives ordinary scale. Wide reveal composed within vertical frame. No people, creatures, text, logos, skulls. Top 15% sky clear for title.

No other people, no creatures, no actual magical portal or glowing symbols, no text or logos. Top 13% and bottom 12% composition quiet for editorial text. She has chosen to destroy the stranger's drawing, not obey it. No Arwen/Arven, no slavery/collars. Refined realistic painterly quality, phone-legible.
